ambiguity_notes: THE MOST DANGEROUS WORD IN THE LATIN IS observabilis. L&S glosses it 'remarkable, observable' and marks it post-Augustan, and its attested uses do not mean 'capable of being observed' in the technical sense of observability theory. The Vulgate citation L&S gives -- Exod. 12.42, 'nox ista est observabilis Domini' -- means 'this is the night TO BE KEPT/celebrated of the Lord', i.e. a night to be religiously OBSERVED. Latin observo carries both 'to watch/note' and 'to keep/observe (a rite, a law)', and observabilis inherits the second. To a Latinist, PARTIM OBSERVABILIS therefore risks reading 'partly remarkable' or 'partly to-be-ritually-kept'. The word is retained for want of a better deverbative, but this trap is live and is the first thing a reviewer should attack.

'Partially observable' is the load-bearing qualifier (CONCEPTS.json) and the reason a recognition density is needed at all. A register that drops 'partim'/'aṃśataḥ' does not name a weaker version of the concept -- it names a DIFFERENT formalism (a plain MDP), in which no belief state and no inference are required. The qualifier is not decoration.

Sanskrit nirṇaya [MW 555,1] leads with 'COMPLETE ascertainment'. That is precisely what a partially observable process denies: in a POMDP the ascertainment is constitutively incomplete. The compound therefore sets its own qualifier fighting its own head noun. This is recorded rather than repaired because every alternative considered was worse; it is the single weakest joint in the Sanskrit entry.

nirṇaya further carries legal 'sentence, verdict' and logical 'deduction, inference' senses [MW 555,1]. The decision in a POMDP is an action selection under uncertainty -- neither a juridical verdict nor a deductive conclusion.

Sanskrit prakriyā [MW 653] carries 'a ceremony, observance, formality' and 'a chapter (esp. the introductory chapter of a work)'. A POMDP is neither a rite nor a book-division. Note the accidental rhyme with the Latin trap above: BOTH registers' words for the process/observing drift toward RITUAL OBSERVANCE. That is a coincidence of two independent lexicons, not evidence of anything, and must not be presented as a finding.

Latin decisio is literally 'a cutting off' (from decīdo) and its figurative sense II is 'a decision, SETTLEMENT, AGREEMENT' -- Cicero's uses are of legal settlements between parties. A POMDP decision is not negotiated and has no counterparty.

'Markov' names a person and imports nothing but the memorylessness property. No register may gloss it descriptively (e.g. as 'memoryless'), because the concept is fixed to the formalism's conventional name, and a descriptive gloss would silently assert which property is meant.

ambiguity_notes: THE CENTRAL TRAP OF THIS ENTRY: a likelihood is NOT a probability of the hidden state. p(o|s) read as a function of s is not a distribution over s and does not normalise over s. Every register word here that means 'how probable the state is' or 'how true it is' names a different object -- the posterior, or worse, a truth-value.

This is why Latin verisimilitudo is fatal and not merely infelicitous. L&S does not even grant it an independent entry; the headword reads 'vērĭsĭmĭlis, vērĭsĭmĭlĭter, and vērĭsĭmĭlĭtūdo, more correctly written separately, vērī simĭlis, etc., v. under verus and similis' -- i.e. the word IS 'veri similis', LIKE THE TRUTH. It asserts likeness-to-truth, which is exactly the assertion a likelihood does not make.

SPANISH AND LATIN DIVERGE HERE, AND THE DIVERGENCE MUST NOT BE LAUNDERED. Spanish has conventionalised 'verosimilitud' for statistical likelihood; Latin has not. The Spanish convention is a fait accompli of usage and is admissible in Spanish on those terms. It may NOT be back-borrowed into Latin on the strength of the cognate: the Latin word's attested semantics actively contradict the concept. A translator who reasons 'Spanish says verosimilitud, so Latin says verisimilitudo' has produced a pseudopropheta by cognate.

Sanskrit pradiś [MW 679,3] carries 'order, command, dominion'. The A tensor commands nothing and has dominion over nothing. These senses are wholly absent from the concept and are live in the attested word.

tantra [MW 436,1-2] is the tempting etymological parallel: MW gives 'a loom', 'the warp', and 'the leading or principal or essential part, main point, characteristic feature, model, type, system, framework'. The loom/warp sense is a genuine semantic cousin of Latin tendo's 'stretch'. It is nevertheless FORBIDDEN (below), because MW's same entry gives 'a class of works teaching magical and mystical formularies'. Using tantra would import the entire Tantric corpus into a likelihood matrix.

CONCEPTS.json: 'ambiguity lives in A, controllability lives in B'. A register that renders A and B with interchangeable words for 'matrix/array' loses the division of labour that makes the pair mean anything.

ambiguity_notes: THE HOMONYM TRAP, AND IT IS SEVERE: MW carries TWO distinct iṣṭa entries. 1. iṣṭa [169,2] from √iṣ = 'sought, wished, desired... cherished'. 2. iṣṭa [169,3] = 'p.p. fr. √yaj' = 'SACRIFICED, WORSHIPPED WITH SACRIFICES'. The two are formally identical in Devanagari and IAST. इष्टप्रत्यक्ष is therefore readable, with full lexical warrant, as 'SACRIFICED OBSERVATION' -- a sacrificial offering of the percept. This is not a strained reading; it is MW's second headword on the facing column. Any use of iṣṭa in a corpus about observations must carry this note.

THE ASYMMETRY IS THE CONCEPT AND NO REGISTER'S WORD CARRIES IT. C is SET, never learned -- OBSERVED in the corpus (01-kitchen-rules M13: learning covers A/B/D/E, never C; grep-confirmed in this repo at cookbook/01-kitchen-rules.md lines 71-72 and 129-130). CONCEPTS.json states the reason: 'A goal that were learned from its own counts would have no purchase; C is where the goal enters from outside.' A register word implying acquisition, habituation, or learning falsifies C outright. This must be carried by the definition, because no word in any of the five registers carries it.

C IS A PRIOR OVER PREFERRED OBSERVATIONS, NOT A GOAL-STATE. This is the second-most-common error after the learning one. The preference is over o, not over s. A register that renders C as 'goal', 'end', 'telos', 'target' asserts a preferred STATE OF THE WORLD; C ranges over what the agent expects to SEE. The distinction is the whole reason C multiplies against the A tensor's outputs rather than the B tensor's.

Latin opto's L&S gloss is 'to choose, SELECT, prefer'. The 'choose/select' senses imply an ACT of choosing between presented alternatives. C is not an act and does not choose; it is a standing distribution, fixed before any alternative is presented. The agent's choosing happens in policy selection, scored against C -- not in C.

Sanskrit iṣṭa 1 [MW 169,2] glosses include 'cherished' and 'desired'. 'Desired' shades toward a felt state. C asserts nothing about feeling. That this corpus's C is fixed by a modulator NAMED 'affect' makes the trap worse, not better: the name is a label on a mechanism, and no register may let it become a claim about experienced desire. TRUE and HONEST signals are sovereign; C is a TRUE-store object and may not be given a lived-experience word.

Spanish 'preferencia' and Hindi 'अभिरुचि' both tend to imply a RANKING among options, and the Hindi word additionally shades toward 'taste, inclination, interest'. C is a distribution, not an ordering and not a taste. A distribution induces an ordering; it is not one.

ambiguity_notes: THE WHOLE POINT IS THAT LEARNING HERE IS COUNTING, NOT DESCENDING. CONCEPTS.json: 'Learning here is counting, not descending.' The corpus enforces it mechanically -- an AST guard rejects autodiff/optax/torch/grad/backward in the loop (M13; visible in this repo at cookbook/01-kitchen-rules.md lines 71-72). Every register's ordinary word for 'learning' in an ML context now connotes gradient descent, because that is what the field does. So every register's natural word actively asserts the thing this concept denies. The registers are fighting the concept, not carrying it.

'Conjugate' is the load-bearing technical qualifier and is the REASON no gradient is needed: conjugacy makes the posterior update closed-form. A register that renders 'Dirichlet learning' and drops 'conjugate' has removed the explanation and left an unexplained assertion. Worse, 'conjugate' is a heavy homonym in every register -- grammatical conjugation, chemical conjugation, complex conjugates, conjugal relations -- and the Bayesian sense is the rarest of them.

Sanskrit gaṇanā [MW 343,3] carries 'considering, supposing' and 'regarding, taking notice of' alongside 'reckoning, counting, calculation'. The concept means the arithmetic count ONLY. The 'considering/supposing' senses would reintroduce exactly the deliberative flavour the mechanism lacks: nothing considers anything; counts are incremented.
gaṇanā also carries 'the being enumerated among' [MW 343,3] -- membership in a class rather than the act of counting. A tensor update is not a membership claim.

The 'lr' (learning rate) in 'counts + lr * sufficient_stat' is a scaling factor on the count increment, NOT a step size along a gradient. Its name is borrowed from gradient methods and is misleading in every register. No register should render 'lr' with a word implying descent or step-size, and the safest course is to leave the formula untranslated -- the math is the fence.

Dirichlet is a person (Peter Gustav Lejeune Dirichlet). No register may gloss the name descriptively. The Devanagari transliteration दिरिक्ले proposed here is itself unverified: the name is French-German and its standard Devanagari form, if one exists, was not checked. ambiguity_notes: THE CONCEPT'S OWN NOTE IS THE FENCE: CONCEPTS.json states "'Hidden' means not directly observable, NOT concealed, secret, or withheld by anyone." There is no agent doing the hiding. Every register has an obvious word for 'hidden' that smuggles a concealer in, and choosing between them is the entire work of this entry.

WHY LATIN latens AND NOT occultus: lateō is marked 'v. n.' in L&S -- verb NEUTER, i.e. intransitive. It means 'to lie hid' as something the subject does, or rather undergoes, with no agent. occultus and absconditus are participles of occulō and abscondō, transitive verbs of actively hiding, and both therefore imply someone who hid the thing. The grammar of the Latin verb, not a stylistic preference, is what selects latens.

parokṣa's OWN GLOSS CONTAINS FOUR SENSES THE CONCEPT DENIES. MW [589]: 'beyond the range of sight, invisible, ABSENT, UNKNOWN, unintelligible', and -- found only on the adversarial re-read of 2026-07-15 -- 'PAST, COMPLETED'. The hidden state is NOT absent -- it is present and doing causal work, which is why it can be inferred at all. It is not unknown in principle -- it is precisely what the recognition density is a belief ABOUT. 'Unintelligible' is worse still: an unintelligible state could not be inferred. And 'past, completed' is worse than all three: s is the CURRENT hidden state, live at time t and causing o right now; a word that reads 'the completed state' names something finished and gone, which is the one thing s must not be. The count in this note previously read 'two' in its heading and 'three' in its body, and both were wrong: the best-attested Sanskrit word carries FOUR wrong senses alongside its one right one.

THE SECRECY OBJECTION THIS ENTRY RAISES AGAINST गूढ APPLIES TO ITS OWN CHOSEN WORD, AND THAT WAS MISSED UNTIL THE ADVERSARIAL RE-READ. This entry rejects gūḍha because MW [360,3] gives 'SECRET, PRIVATE' -- i.e. it posits a concealer, which the concept forbids. But MW's parokṣa entry [589] carries, in its own adverbial forms: parokṣeṇa 'out of sight, SECRETLY, mysteriously'; parokṣāt 'SECRETLY, without the knowledge of'; parokṣam 'out of sight, BEHIND ONE'S BACK, in the absence or WITHOUT THE KNOWLEDGE OF'; parokṣe 'BEHIND THE BACK OF'. 'Behind one's back' and 'without the knowledge of' are not merely secrecy-adjacent -- they are agentive: they presuppose a party FROM WHOM something is kept. That is the precise implicature the concept's own fence forbids ('NOT concealed, secret, or withheld by anyone') and the precise ground on which this entry rejects gūḍha. The defence available is narrow and must not be overstated: the ADJECTIVE parokṣa in its lead sense is agent-neutral ('beyond the range of sight'), and it is the adjective, not the adverbs, that enters parokṣāvasthā. But the adverbial senses are in the same entry, they are the forms a reader meets most often in texts, and they establish that Sanskrit parokṣa is NOT the clean agent-free word this entry represented it as. The Latin rendering has a real structural defence here that the Sanskrit does not: lateō's intransitivity is a GRAMMATICAL fact about the verb that excludes an agent, whereas parokṣa's agent-neutrality is only a fact about which sense one selects. STATUS LATENS is therefore better grounded than parokṣāvasthā, and this entry previously implied they were equally strong.

ambiguity_notes: THE ACT/DATUM SPLIT IS THE FIRST TRAP AND IT CATCHES THREE REGISTERS. The concept is the QUANTITY o that arrived -- a datum, a thing. It is not the act of observing. Latin observatio, Spanish observación and Hindi प्रेक्षण all name the act primarily (Spanish softens this with 'accion Y EFECTO de'). This is why the Latin here is OBSERVATUM (the thing observed) and not observatio, and it is the one place in this file where the coined form is clearly better than the attested alternative.

THE PRAMĀṆA PROBLEM, AND IT MAY BE FATAL TO THE SANSKRIT. In Nyāya, pratyakṣa is the first of the pramāṇas -- the MEANS OF VALID KNOWLEDGE. The word does not merely name a percept; in its technical use it certifies the percept as veridical. But o is 'the quantity that ACTUALLY ARRIVED at the sensor' -- arrival, not validity. A sensor can deliver a corrupt, noisy, or miscalibrated reading and it is still o; that is precisely why the A tensor is needed and why ambiguity lives in A. Rendering OBSERVATION as pratyakṣa therefore risks asserting that every observation is valid knowledge -- a metaphysical claim the corpus must not make, and one that would quietly dissolve the whole point of a likelihood. This is the exact hazard CONCEPTS.json names ('Sanskrit philosophical vocabulary carries DOCTRINAL FREIGHT... no translation choice may quietly assert a metaphysics') and the operator's charter names ('Do not assume Sanskrit automatically prevents ambiguity'). 'Evidence' is an evidentiary/probative word: it says the percept ESTABLISHES something. o establishes nothing -- it is what arrived, veridical or not, and a corrupt sensor reading is still o. So the validity implicature this note feared is visible in MW's plain lexical glosses, without any appeal to Nyāya. State the evidence grades separately and do not merge them: the LEXICAL evidentiary sense is now CITED [MW 674,2]; the NYĀYA-pramāṇa doctrinal claim remains UNVERIFIED and flagged. The first is sufficient on its own to keep the rendering under examination. The re-read also found 'superintendence of, care for' -- a supervisory sense wholly absent from the concept; o supervises nothing.

pratyakṣa's LEXICAL SENSE IS OCULAR ('present before the EYES', MW 674,2; the word is literally prati + akṣa, 'before the eye'). o is whatever arrived at ANY sensor -- a thermometer reading, a byte count, an interoceptive hardware signal (M12). THE BRIDGE NOTE, WHICH IS THIS CONCEPT'S REASON FOR EXISTING: CONCEPTS.json says o in an equation and a receipt in a ledger are 'the same kind of object, which is why a confabulated observation corrupts the model rather than merely embarrassing the author'. Any register that renders o as a mere 'impression', 'appearance', or 'sense-datum' -- something mental and private -- severs that bridge. The word must be able to denote a LOGGED, EXTERNAL, CHECKABLE thing, because a receipt is one.

Latin observō carries 'to watch FOR, seek to catch' [L&S] -- purposive, anticipatory watching. o is passive arrival; nothing is sought. The verb also carries the 'keep/observe a rite or law' sense that makes observabilis so treacherous in POMDP.

If pratyakṣa is struck on pramāṇa grounds, parokṣāvasthā loses its lexicographic anchor and BOTH entries must be re-cut together.
